prerequisites: None. Competences taught in the Algorithms and Data Structures module are recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: The students can describe concepts for extending object-relational database systems for geo-applications.
The students can explain principles of fundamental algorithms and data structures for geo-databases.
The students can describe data models for geo-data.
The students can apply query processing in geo-databases.
The students can handle geo-information systems and geo-database systems.
The students are able to apply scientific working methods to independently recognize, formulate, and solve problems.
The students are able to speak freely about scientific content, both in front of an audience and in a discussion.

syllabus_topics: Modeling of geo-data: Vector data and raster data

assessment_methods.method: Oral presentation of solutions for at least two exercise assignments

assessment_rules: Grading is based on a point scale from 0 to 15, according to the examination regulations for the M.Sc. Computer Science degree program. To acquire credit points, students must achieve at least 50 percent of the points from the weekly exercise assignments and orally present the solution of at least two of the exercise assignments. The examination performance can be either an oral individual examination or a written examination.

M. Berg, M. Kreveld, M. Overmars, O. Schwarzkopf: Computational Geometry, Springer.
